newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 2.4 pct in Feb - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 2.4 pct in Feb - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 2.4 percent in the four weeks of fiscal February versus January, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 5.6 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales advanced 5.1 percent in the week ended March 1 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
February was "a pretty good month, maybe an excellent month," said Jay Meltzer, managing director of Redbook Research, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Retailers very nearly hit the relatively high sales targets they had set for the month, and stores appear to expect decent sales performance in March, Meltzer said.
"We will have a few days after Easter where you really don't do much business, but ... it'll still be a good month, hopefully about as good as was February," he said.
Higher-priced merchandise continued to sell well last month, Meltzer said. "The higher-prices, designer-label product is still very much in demand."
